text:
The data point to late 2017. Fed funds is about 1.16%, which fits October or November 2017 (the December 2017 hike took it to about 1.3%). Unemployment of 4.4% is a bit high for those months, since it was 4.1–4.2% by then, but 4.4% fits mid-2017.

Checking other months: in June 2017 fed funds averaged about 1.04%, and in July 1.15%. In August it was 1.16% and in September 1.15%. October was 1.15% and November 1.16%. Unemployment was 4.3% in July and 4.4% in August 2017 after a 4.4% reading in May. The 10-year yield at 2.31% fits August (2.12%), September (2.33%) or October (2.38%). The 2-year at 1.45% fits September 2017 (about 1.47%).

The 12-month changes also fit September 2017. Fed funds was 0.29% in September 2016, so the 12m change is +0.87. The VIX at 9.55 fits September 2017. Treasuries fell 1.3% in the month, consistent with September when yields rose. Gold fell 2.2% in September 2017. Unemployment was 4.2% in September 2017 as first published, though a later vintage may differ, and the snapshot's 4.40 could reflect the figure known at that point. I'll go with September.
